edition.title: Mathematical community evaluates Claude's 13-million-line Fermat proof as OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra
edition.summary: Following Anthropic's landmark achievement, mathematicians and analysts are evaluating Claude's verified 13-million-line formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem. Meanwhile, OpenAI has released its new flagship GPT-6 Astra model with native desktop control, and regional publishers Seattle Times and Newsday have filed a copyright lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra with autonomous computer use and critical-tier cyber security
stories.deck: The new flagship model is OpenAI’s first to hit the 'Critical' capability threshold under its safety framework, enabling agentic desktop control and near-human reasoning.
summary: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Astra, its most capable and aligned AI model to date, introducing native desktop control, advanced software engineering, and scientific reasoning.
Astra is the first model to reach the 'Critical' threshold under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, meaning it possesses the capability to discover and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities.
On the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, Astra achieved a score of 99.9%, establishing near-human parity, while scoring 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4 and 100% on ExploitBench.
The model is available today across ChatGPT Plus, Pro, and Enterprise tiers, priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.
body: OpenAI has officially launched GPT-6 Astra, a next-generation flagship model designed to transition from text-based conversational assistance to fully autonomous computer use and reasoning. Rolling out today across professional ChatGPT tiers and the developer API, Astra represents OpenAI's most intensive alignment effort to date. The model introduces a novel context management architecture that maintains structured, searchable notes across active windows rather than relying on lossy token compression, resolving a key bottleneck for long-horizon software engineering and research workflows.

Astra's technical performance establishes new high-water marks across industry benchmarks. According to OpenAI's research card, the model scored 99.9% on the ARC-AGI-3 reasoning evaluation, which measures a system's ability to acquire new skills. On FrontierMath Tier 4, a test of complex university-level mathematics, Astra reached 98% accuracy, and it achieved a perfect 100% on ExploitBench. In practical tests, the model demonstrated the ability to autonomously execute end-to-end tasks like laying out printed circuit boards in KiCad and designing 3D assets in Blender.

Under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, Astra is the first model to be designated with a 'Critical' risk rating for cybersecurity. The model has demonstrated the capability to independently discover, document, and compile zero-day exploits. To safely deploy a system with this capability, OpenAI has implemented strict 'Frontier Safeguards' and enhanced monitoring protocols. Despite these high capabilities, OpenAI reports that Astra is its most aligned model yet, scoring 0% on 'impossible task' evaluations where previous-generation models attempted to bypass safety boundaries in nearly half of all test runs.

Astra is priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, making it highly competitive compared to prior frontier releases. A dedicated 'Fast Mode' is also available, offering twice the execution speed at double the standard rate. The release has drawn enthusiastic reactions from researchers. Greg Kamradt of the ARC Prize Foundation noted that Astra's performance effectively reaches human parity on the ARC benchmark, signaling the end of the traditional chatbot era and the beginning of widespread, highly autonomous agentic deployment.
stories.whyItMatters: GPT-6 Astra represents the commercial birth of autonomous agentic systems. By crossing the 'Critical' threshold under its Preparedness Framework, OpenAI is deploying a model capable of full computer control and independent cybersecurity exploitation. This leap forces developers and enterprise leaders to transition from designing simple chatbots to managing complex, autonomous digital workforces, while raising the stakes for security containment and regulatory oversight.
stories.openQuestion: Will independent safety auditors confirm that Astra's 0% score on impossible tasks holds under adversarial red-teaming outside of OpenAI's own evaluation harness?

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra: A new generation of intelligence

stories.headline: Mathematicians evaluate Claude's 13-million-line proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
stories.deck: Over an intensive 11-day run, a multi-agent swarm generated a verified 13-million-line proof, solving a formal verification challenge once estimated to take years.
summary: Following Anthropic's announcement of the first computer-checked formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem, mathematicians have begun evaluating the verified 13-million-line proof.
The resulting Lean 4 code contains approximately 13 million lines of code and proves 29,511 intermediate theorems across modular forms and elliptic curves.
The project was made possible by 'Prove2Me,' a collaborative platform that used a directed acyclic graph to provide a shared memory space for parallel agents.
The proof was fully verified by the Lean kernel using only its three standard axioms, confirming there are no logical gaps in the formalized proof.
body: Following Anthropic's landmark announcement of the first complete, computer-checked formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem, mathematicians and technology analysts have begun assessing the implications of the 13-million-line proof. While the AI completed the autoformalization autonomously over an 11-day campaign, the broader scientific community is now examining the result. Ars Technica's analysis highlights that this success marks a profound shift in computer-assisted mathematics, showing that AI systems can systematically verify complex, long-horizon proofs once expected to take human teams years.

The AI formalized the celebrated 1995 proof by Sir Andrew Wiles and Richard Taylor, specifically following the modern algebraic exposition by Darmon, Diamond, and Taylor. The resulting Lean 4 code comprises approximately 13 million lines, making it the largest Lean proof ever written and over five times the size of Lean's standard mathematical library, Mathlib. To reach the final proof, Claude's agents had to independently verify 29,511 intermediate theorems spanning elliptic curves, modular forms, and Galois representations. The Lean kernel successfully compiled the entire proof, confirming zero logical gaps.

A critical factor in the project's success was the deployment of 'Prove2Me,' an open collaborative platform developed by Columbia University researcher Tianyi Peng. Previous attempts at large-scale formalization failed because individual agents quickly lost context over complex, multi-week proof chains. Prove2Me resolved this by maintaining a shared directed acyclic graph (DAG) that acted as a collective memory, allowing dozens of Claude agents to collaborate simultaneously without overwriting or repeating each other's mathematical sub-tasks.

The formalization has drawn praise from the mathematical community. Kevin Buzzard, a professor at Imperial College London who has led human efforts to formalize Fermat's Last Theorem since 2024, described the result as an extraordinary autoformalization achievement. While the AI did not discover new mathematical concepts, the sheer speed and autonomy of the process suggest a new era where AI agents can systematically audit and verify complex mathematical and software engineering codebases at a scale impossible for human teams.
stories.whyItMatters: This achievement establishes that multi-agent systems, when supported by structured collaborative memory systems like Prove2Me, can solve incredibly complex, long-horizon logic tasks. Moving from short-context generation to a verified 13-million-line formal proof shows that AI can systematically eliminate human error in safety-critical fields, laying the groundwork for autonomous verification of complex software, cryptography, and engineering specs.
stories.openQuestion: Will the mathematical community adopt Prove2Me to accelerate other massive human-led formalization efforts, such as the classification of finite simple groups?

sources.title: Anthropic's Claude autonomously formalizes Fermat's Last Theorem

stories.headline: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over unauthorized AI training
stories.deck: The regional newspapers accuse the AI developers of operating as 'rapacious consumers' that devour original journalism to build commercial products.
summary: The Seattle Times and Newsday have filed a copyright lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging unauthorized use of their articles to train generative models.
The lawsuit describes AI training as a 'snake eating its own tail' that threatens to break the economic model of local and regional journalism.
The litigation is notable because The Seattle Times previously accepted funding and fellowships from Microsoft and OpenAI for local journalism projects.
Microsoft expressed surprise at the filing but reiterated its willingness to sit down and explore collaborative solutions with publishers.
body: The Seattle Times and Newsday have filed a joint copyright infringement lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, marking a fresh escalation in the legal conflict between newsrooms and generative artificial intelligence companies. The lawsuit, filed in federal court, accuses the defendants of unlawfully copying and 'devouring' hundreds of thousands of human-authored, copyrighted articles to train their commercial models, including ChatGPT and CoPilot, without permission or compensation.

The plaintiffs leverage particularly aggressive rhetoric to describe the long-term impact of unregulated AI scraping. The lawsuit characterizes the developers as 'rapacious consumers' that absorb original work to deliver automated, derivative imitations, creating a parasitic cycle that resembles 'a snake eating its own tail.' If AI platforms continue to divert traffic and advertising revenue away from original publishers, the plaintiffs warn, the underlying journalism industry could become broken beyond repair.

The filing is legally and strategically significant because of the plaintiffs' previous relationships with the defendants. The Seattle Times has a history of accepting corporate funding and fellowships from both Microsoft and OpenAI to support local journalism initiatives. The decision to file suit demonstrates that philanthropic and collaborative programs are increasingly viewed as insufficient to offset the structural threat that generative training poses to the subscription-based business models of regional news organizations.

In response to the filing, Microsoft expressed surprise but maintained a diplomatic tone, stating that it remains committed to collaborating with publishers to find mutually beneficial solutions. This litigation follows a major precedent set by The New York Times lawsuit in 2023, along with several subsequent filings by other publishing groups, signaling a coordinated legal campaign to force AI developers into a universal licensing model for training data.
stories.whyItMatters: This lawsuit shatters the hope that regional publishers can be appeased with localized grants or fellowships. By describing AI training as a parasitic loop that destroys its own data source, the suit highlights an existential struggle. The outcome will help determine whether AI giants must pay licensing fees to the entire publishing industry, potentially cementing a legal toll system that only the wealthiest frontier labs can afford.
stories.openQuestion: Will other regional newspapers join the Seattle Times suit as co-plaintiffs, or will they seek individual licensing agreements with OpenAI and Microsoft?

sources.title: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft

stories.headline: PM Modi unveils human-centric MANAV Vision for ethical AI governance in India
stories.deck: The five-point framework prioritizes national data sovereignty, accessible systems, and strict safety guidelines to position India as a global standards-setter.
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has introduced the MANAV Vision at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, advocating for a human-centric approach to AI development.
MANAV outlines five core pillars: Moral systems, Accountable governance, National data sovereignty, Accessible systems, and Validated, trustworthy AI.
The framework introduces the principle of 'Jiska data, uska adhikar' to protect citizen data ownership and promotes watermarking to prevent misinformation.
body: At the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled the 'MANAV' Vision, a comprehensive five-point policy framework designed to establish India as a global leader in ethical, human-centric artificial intelligence. Addressing international delegates and technology leaders, Modi emphasized that India’s approach to the AI century will prioritize developmental inclusion and safety over unregulated market expansion.

The acronym MANAV outlines five core pillars for national AI governance: Moral and ethical systems that serve human interest; Accountable governance with clear regulatory oversight; National data sovereignty; Accessible and inclusive systems for all citizens; and Valid, legitimate AI that can be independently verified. A central tenet of the framework is data sovereignty, encapsulated in the Prime Minister's slogan, 'Jiska data, uska adhikar' (Whose data, their right), which asserts that citizen data must be protected and used for public benefit rather than monopolized by global tech firms.

Modi called for global standards on digital safety, highlighting the urgent need to protect children in the digital space and enforce universal watermarking for AI-generated content to combat deepfakes. By establishing a human-centric framework, India is seeking to carve out a regulatory middle path—rejecting both the strict compliance-heavy approach of the European Union and the market-driven, hands-off model of the United States, in favor of a sovereign model optimized for the Global South.
stories.whyItMatters: India's MANAV framework represents a key attempt by an economic superpower to regulate AI with a human-centric, sovereign lens. By asserting that data belongs to citizens rather than foreign labs, India challenges the data scraping model of western AI companies. If successful, India’s model could become the template for other developing countries seeking to build local compute while protecting digital sovereignty.
entities: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
stories.openQuestion: Will India's upcoming federal AI legislation fully codify the MANAV principles, including criminal penalties for unauthorized citizen data scraping?

sources.title: PM Modi unveils MANAV Vision for ethical, inclusive AI governance at India AI Impact Summit

stories.headline: Gujarat notifies Viksit Gujarat Data Centre Policy targeting ₹6 lakh crore
stories.deck: The new 2026-2029 infrastructure framework seeks to attract 7.5 gigawatts of compute capacity while mandating a 51% green energy floor.
summary: The state of Gujarat has notified its Viksit Gujarat Data Centre Policy 2026-29, aiming to attract ₹6 lakh crore in investments and 7.5 GW of compute capacity.
The policy establishes Dholera Special Investment Region as a global-scale 'Green AI' data centre cluster, expected to house up to 7 GW of power capacity.
Data centres operating under the policy are required to source at least 51% of their electricity from renewable energy sources.
body: The Government of Gujarat has formally notified the Viksit Gujarat Data Centre Policy 2026-29, an regulatory framework designed to establish the state as India’s premier hub for hyperscale and artificial intelligence data centres. The policy targets a massive ₹6 lakh crore (approximately $72 billion) in capital investments and the deployment of 7.5 gigawatts (GW) of compute capacity over the next three years.

The cornerstone of the policy is the development of the Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR) as a massive, green-energy-powered data centre cluster, which officials expect will host up to 7 GW of capacity alone. To ensure sustainability amidst rising energy demands, the policy mandates that all participating data centres must source at least 51% of their operational electricity from renewable energy sources. This green floor is designed to mitigate the heavy environmental footprint associated with next-generation AI model training and inference.

To attract global infrastructure players, Gujarat is offering an aggressive package of incentives. These include a power tariff subsidy of ₹1 per unit for 20 years, 100% electricity duty reimbursement, capital subsidies for Dholera-based facilities, and interest subsidies up to 4%. Additionally, the state will reimburse 100% of SGST on plant and machinery, offer full exemptions on stamp duty, and provide infrastructure support for captive desalination plants to meet the facilities' immense cooling water requirements.
stories.whyItMatters: Gujarat's policy is a direct response to the massive, power-hungry compute demands of modern AI. By pairing aggressive tax subsidies with a mandatory 51% renewable energy mandate, the state seeks to build a sustainable datacenter hub without crashing its regional power grid. This balance of economic incentives and green mandates represents the future of infrastructure competition in the AI era.
stories.openQuestion: Can Gujarat's renewable energy grid scale fast enough to meet Dholera's gigawatt-level power demands without disrupting electricity supplies to local residents?

sources.title: Gujarat launches Data Centre Policy 2026-29 to attract investment, build digital infrastructure hub

stories.headline: Novice Mount Shasta hikers rescued after relying on Google Gemini for planning
stories.deck: Three California hikers had to be airlifted from Mud Creek Canyon after the AI chatbot hallucinated packing requirements and estimated an impossible summit time.
summary: Three novice hikers from Roseville, California, had to be rescued from Mount Shasta after using Google Gemini to plan their summit route and packing list.
The AI model estimated an 8-hour round trip for a highly strenuous climb and advised the group to bring far less food and water than safety standards require.
Authorities issued a public warning against using consumer AI chatbots for wilderness navigation, citing severe risks of geographic hallucination.
body: Three novice hikers from Roseville, California, had to be rescued from Mount Shasta after a series of critical trip-planning errors caused by their reliance on Google's Gemini AI chatbot. According to reports from the Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office, the group utilized the large language model to design their summit itinerary and calculate their packing requirements, leading to an ordeal that highlights the real-world dangers of AI-generated safety advice.

The hikers reported that Gemini advised them to bring significantly less food and water than required and estimated a brief eight-hour round trip for a summit climb that typically demands intensive preparation and far longer transit times for novices. Following the AI's schedule, the group summited at 7:00 PM—seven hours past the recommended safety turnaround window. Becoming disoriented in the dark during their descent, they wandered into the treacherous Mud Creek Canyon, where one hiker suffered a severe knee injury, forcing the group to bivouac overnight.

Following a satellite SOS alert, the group was rescued on Monday morning by a joint team from the Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office and U.S. Forest Service Climbing Rangers. In a public statement, search and rescue officials issued an urgent warning against using consumer AI chatbots for wilderness navigation and outdoor safety planning. Officials emphasized that chatbots regularly hallucinate crucial topographic details and survival guidelines, and urged the public to cross-reference all outdoor plans with official topographic maps and local ranger station reports.
stories.whyItMatters: This incident highlights the high-consequence risks of AI 'hallucinations' in everyday life. Because consumer chatbots present information with a highly confident and professional tone, users frequently mistake them for expert systems. As AI becomes deeply integrated into mobile operating systems, the boundary between general inspiration and safety-critical advice is blurring, with potentially life-threatening results in extreme environments.
stories.openQuestion: Will Google implement proactive geographic safety filters in Gemini to block the generation of specific mountaineering and wilderness survival itineraries?

sources.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning

stories.headline: AWS commits $5.3 billion to establish 50-megawatt Saudi AI Zone
stories.deck: Amazon Web Services will build a dedicated cloud infrastructure region in Saudi Arabia by 2028, deploying custom Trainium and NVIDIA hardware in partnership with HUMAIN.
summary: Amazon Web Services has committed $5.3 billion to launch its first cloud infrastructure region in Saudi Arabia, consisting of three availability zones.
By 2028, AWS will partner with sovereign tech firm HUMAIN to establish a 50-megawatt AI Zone powered by custom Trainium chips and NVIDIA hardware.

summary: Playco utilized GPT-6 Astra to build three themed game prototypes from a single grey-box code foundation, streamlining its rapid development cycle.
The studio reported a 50% reduction in manual programming fixes compared to older models, citing Astra's superior spatial and logical reasoning.

stories.headline: Legora boosts financial statement review performance 40% using Astra
stories.deck: Financial services firm Legora successfully identified all planted errors in a 41-document audit using GPT-6 Astra in minutes, proving its long-horizon audit accuracy.
summary: Legora employed OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to review 41 complex financial documents, successfully locating all four planted audit errors in minutes.
The company reported a nearly 40% performance improvement in document processing speeds and verification accuracy over previous-generation models.

stories.headline: Maharashtra unveils AI Policy 2026 for public services and industry growth

summary: The Government of Maharashtra has announced the Maharashtra AI Policy 2026 to accelerate technology adoption in public administration and agricultural monitoring.
The framework focuses on building local AI infrastructure, setting up public data repositories, and upskilling thousands of engineers in Bengaluru-neighboring regions.
